name: New Mexico River Stewardship Program

funder.name: New Mexico Environment Department, Surface Water Quality Bureau

administered_by.name: New Mexico Environment Department, Surface Water Quality Bureau

summary: State funding, awarded through requests for proposals, for planning, design and construction of projects that improve surface water quality or river habitat on New Mexico streams and rivers. Nonprofits, businesses, local governments and Tribes can apply.
reporting: Funded projects must submit project reports under NMED's reporting guidance.

steps: Submit proposal through the state procurement system

eligibility.rule: Project delivers on-the-ground restoration, including if it seeks planning funds
Project does more than standalone monitoring
Private-land project passes anti-donation review by the evaluation committee and State Board of Finance
Has a public, active SAM.gov registration in good standing
Is a New Mexico registered vendor and either a state-registered business or a government entity

documents: Letter of support from the project landowner

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include: towns, cities, counties, soil and water conservation districts, irrigation districts, state agencies, non-profit and for-profit organizations, Indian Nations, Pueblos and Tribes.

co_finance_required.quote: No, there is no match requirement for supplying, identifying and tracking matching funds.

reporting.quote: All funding opportunities provided by NMED SWQB require project reports.

effort.quote: Projects are selected through Requests for Proposals (RFP) using the state procurement system.
An evaluation committee will rank proposals based on evaluation criteria stated within the RFP.
will implement a risk assessment evaluation of all awardees prior to making an award and after the project is complete.

eligibility.quote: Currently, funds can be used to pay for planning within the context of completing an on-the-ground restoration project but not for planning as the exclusive end-product (such as developing a watershed plan).
Although monitoring is important to improving surface water quality it is not the primary focus of the River Stewardship Program and cannot be funded as a standalone project.
Projects on private lands may be eligible if they pass an anti-donation clause review by the Evaluation Committee and State Board of Finance.
Entities must also be registered on SAM.gov and have a public, active profile in good standing.

In order to establish a contract with the State of New Mexico, an Offeror must register as a vendor for the state with the New Mexico Department of Finance and Administration and either be a registered business with the New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department or be a government entity.

after_award.quote: All funding opportunities provided by NMED SWQB require project reports.
Progress reports are due July 31st and January 31st for the prior reporting period (January 1st - June 30th and July 1st - December 31st, respectively) for each year that the contract is valid.

documents.quote: Yes, letters of support must be included by the landowner where the project will occur.
